# Results — Study 229 (Beneish M-score) on real EDGAR + yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Beneish M-score
computed annually from EDGAR 10-K fundamentals (fiscal year *t*) and study-local
EDGAR caches for AR and PPE. Forward return = calendar year *t+1*. Panel:
current S&P 500 members projected back — **survivorship-biased**; results are
upper bounds. As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Coverage | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| EDGAR shared (_edgar_*.parquet) | 2007–2024 | 9 concepts | — |
| EDGAR local (_cache/*.parquet) | 2007–2024 | AR + PPE, 161 common tickers | `872f820dc631` |
| _edgar_yrret.parquet | 1962–2026 | forward returns | — |

M-score panel: **15 years × up to 161 tickers**, **1,089 valid firm-year pairs** (year with returns).

**Fallback rules** (disclosed): GMI = 1.0 when GrossProfit absent; SGAI = 1.0 when GrossProfit absent;
DSRI = 1.0 when AR absent; AQI/DEPI = 1.0 when PPE absent; LTD = 0 when not reported.
These conservative neutral-value fallbacks expand coverage while slightly biasing components toward 1.0.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Hedge mean (Low-M − High-M) | **+0.87%/yr** |
| Hedge volatility | 7.35%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | 0.12 |
| Bootstrap 95% CI on Sharpe | [−0.27, +0.70] |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.65** |
| Hit rate (years with positive hedge) | 60% (9/15) |
| n years | 15 |

## Per-bucket annual means

| Bucket | Mean return/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Low-M (clean)** | +19.0% | +7.76 |
| Mid-M (grey zone) | +14.9% | +7.47 |
| **High-M (manipulators)** | +18.2% | +6.81 |
| Market EW | +17.4% | +8.16 |

*The spread (+0.9pp) is smaller than one year of noise (7.4%/vol). All three buckets
return roughly 15–19%/yr — driven by the bull market of 2009–2023, not by M-score sorting.*

## Firm-level cross-section

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Total firm-year pairs | 1,089 |
| Pearson corr(M, next-yr return) | **+0.051** |
| M > −1.78 (likely manipulators) | 13.0% of obs |
| M ≤ −1.78 (clean) | 87.0% of obs |
| Mean M-score | −2.43 |
| Median M-score | −2.69 |
| Fingerprint | `872f820dc631` |

Note: the positive firm-level correlation (+0.051) means higher-M firms tend to earn
*more* the following year — the *opposite* of what the manipulation-detection theory
predicts. This is consistent with the survivorship-biased universe where genuine
manipulators (who would blow up) are absent.

## Survivorship-bias caveat

The EDGAR panel uses *current* S&P 500 membership projected backwards. Firms that were
caught manipulating earnings, delisted, or went bankrupt are **absent** — which
systematically deflates the apparent short-M edge. In reality, those high-M manipulators
are exactly the firms that would have blown up and made the short leg profitable.
The +0.87%/yr gross hedge is almost certainly an underestimate of what a truly unbiased
implementation would find — but the signal is still too noisy to trade.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Hedge HAC t = +0.65, far below the ±2 inference bar.
  Firm-level correlation = +0.051 (opposite sign to theory). In the survivorship-biased
  S&P 500 universe, the Beneish M-score does not reliably predict cross-sectional returns.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The tiny gross spread (+0.87%/yr) would be wiped out by
  transaction costs, short-selling costs (borrow fees on the high-M leg), and the
  survivorship-bias adjustment. No trade.
- **Myth-check — MIXED.** Beneish's original paper showed detection power for known
  manipulators in a biased sample. Out-of-sample on the S&P 500 survivor universe,
  the return signal is absent. The score detects manipulation risk; it does not
  translate to equity alpha.
